text:
I can say without a shadow of a doubt that selling my car to fund my time at The Dawn was the absolute best decision of my entire life.

Healing is rarely ever supposed to be comfortable. In a community setting like this, you will run into every type of personality that exists in the outside world, often in its most extreme form. Other clients will complain, and the process will feel incredibly challenging at times. But there is a profound, undeniable healing that happens through authentic connection. Here, I learned to get used to discomfort, to finally speak aloud the things heavily tied to guilt, shame, anxiety, and fear. I learned that it is okay to say the wrong thing, and that true growth happens when you allow yourself to drop the mask and be seen.

The staff and doctors here are elite professionals who intimately understand the mechanics of trauma:

Robert, my focus therapist, is genuinely the best therapist I have ever had in my entire life.

Helen, the clinical director, proved to be not only an exceptionally skilled practitioner in the healing process during our brief talks, but also an avid, inspiring leader.

The entire staff, from the nurses to the support team, is incredibly polite, compassionate, and professional. In two months, I did not encounter a single person who showed attitude or didn't want to be here.

I chose the Viva package (off-site residence) for two months, though due to renovations, I spent the first six weeks on-site. While the Viva accommodations are perfectly good enough to get the job done, staying on-site is incredibly useful because it gives you immediate access to professional help, nurses, and medications at odd hours of the night. Furthermore, being on-site allowed me to utilize the amenities, like the gym and the piano, for an extra two hours a day, which is surprisingly worth it.

Every single aspect of the programming is intentionally tailored toward mental health and nervous system regulation. The activities, including TRE (Trauma Releasing Exercises), sound healing, massage, yoga, and Muay Thai kickboxing, are purposeful. Even the food is scientifically part of the narrative. Having studied nutrition for mood stability myself, I immediately noticed the intentional inclusion of beets, pumpkin seeds, and dried apricots. Furthermore, when the intense "cycle" of processing trauma triggered massive cravings for carbohydrates and chocolate, I was incredibly grateful that the dining room always had cookies and snacks on hand, and that the store had plenty of treats to help.

If you are considering coming here for trauma, I HIGHLY recommend booking 56 days over 28. That extension grants you access to the specialized trauma group. You absolutely need those first 28 days in the regular groups just to stabilize, understand the process, and learn how the community works before diving into the deepest layers of your past.  I thought I learned everything I needed until I entered the second group, and I couldn't believe how much deeper the path of connection and acceptance could go.

It may not feel comfortable every day, but please trust that this place knows exactly what they are doing. I am leaving with a sense of groundedness I didn't think was possible, and I cannot wait to see where life takes me from here.

— Joseph

text: The Dawn gave me a sense peace & presence that I didn't think was possible. The therapists work hard to help you realise the roots of issues & I am incredibly grateful for my time here. Like everything, what you put in is what you get out, & I thrived on gaining insight on my mental health through the psycho educational, relapse prevention classes, alongside a 1-1 therapist. (The people it doesn't work for are usually the ones not putting their all in, not attending groups, not focused on making real changes in their everyday lives). The support staff, medical team, & everyone working there give so much to the clients in terms of friendliness, kindest & respect.

Had the opportunity to visit The Dawn for the first time and learn more about its rehabilitation program—a place where people come to heal, reflect, and recover from various traumatic experiences.

What struck me most was the atmosphere. Nestled among the natural beauty of Chiang Mai, The Dawn feels more like a sanctuary than a treatment center. Peaceful, serene, and thoughtfully designed, it offers an environment where anyone seeking recovery can truly focus on finding their path toward healing and renewal.

My experience at The Dawn Rehab Centre in Chiang Mai has been nothing short of life-changing. When I arrived, I was struggling deeply with addiction and trauma, unsure of who I was or how to move forward. After completing a 12-week bespoke program, I can genuinely say that I feel like a completely different person;  grounded, empowered, and truly ready to step back into the real world.

A huge part of this transformation is thanks to the incredible people who supported me every step of the way. My focal therapist, Alan Wood, guided me with compassion, insight, and unwavering care. His approach helped me confront the core of my issues and rebuild myself from a place of understanding rather than shame.

I also want to express my gratitude to Helen Wells, the Clinical Director, whose leadership and vision shape the remarkable therapeutic environment at The Dawn. Her presence and expertise were felt throughout the entire program.

The support team was equally extraordinary. I want to thank David, Abdulla, Pang, Jack, Top, Bas, Ping, Nora, Mary, Beam, Mun and Linh each of you played a unique role in my healing. Whether it was a conversation, a smile, or guidance during difficult moments, your kindness made all the difference.

And to the amazing admissions team, Alex Holland, Marcus, Daryl, and everyone else involved, thank you for making the process smooth, reassuring, and filled with genuine care from the very beginning.

The entire staff at The Dawn work together like a family, and during my stay, I truly felt part of that family. The environment, the personalized therapy, the structure, and the warmth of the community created the perfect space for deep healing and growth.

I leave The Dawn with clarity, confidence, and a renewed sense of purpose. This journey has changed my life in ways I will forever be grateful for.

Thank you, The Dawn. You gave me my life back.

This was my second experience of residential treatment. I arrived with an understanding of what therapeutic work involved, but not what this specific process would ask of me. I planned to stay four to six weeks. I stayed several months.

I arrived at The Dawn numb and in a state of near emotional paralysis. A few years of recovery under my belt, yet more disconnected from myself than ever.

The setting itself is inherently healing: beautiful grounds, comfortable accommodation, and a holistic programme that attends to the whole person. It is a genuinely good place to do hard work.

It's worth noting that The Dawn isn't only for people in early recovery. I came seeking deeper psychological work, and the facility was fully equipped for that. The therapeutic offering goes well beyond addiction treatment. The work here is serious and substantive. I was able to engage with a range of modalities, including somatic work, held by clinicians who clearly understand that recovery isn't just about the mind. The emphasis on reconnecting with the body, not just processing cognitively, made a profound difference for me.

This isn't a facility that offers one-size-fits-all treatment. The team took time to understand what I needed and built something around that. And when I had feedback, it was genuinely listened to and, where appropriate, acted upon.

There were moments during my time at The Dawn where I couldn't see a future waiting for me on the other side of the gates. As is often true of any meaningful therapeutic process, things got worse before they got better. And they got better.

I leave equipped with the skills to sit in discomfort rather than run from it, to move towards a fulfilling life rather than away from myself, towards a future aligned with my values and one that doesn't require me to contort myself into impossible positions (unless on a yoga mat).

After a lifetime of jumping from buoy to buoy, fighting the tides, I seem finally to have learned to swim with rather than against them. I'm not looking for the next goal, but moving in a direction. And much like The Dawn itself, all I have to do is keep showing up. To everyone at The Dawn, thank you for all that you do.

Coming to The Dawn for 90 days was the first time I felt truly safe enough to face my trauma rather than just manage the symptoms. The structure, consistency, and depth of the work allowed me to slow down and understand how much my past was shaping my reactions, relationships, and self-worth. What stood out most was that the team didn’t rush me or offer quick fixes—they stayed with me through the difficult parts, helping me build emotional regulation, trust, and healthier coping patterns. By the end of my stay, I didn’t feel “fixed,” but I felt grounded, clearer, and finally equipped with the tools and insight to move forward with my life in a very different way.

I visited The Dawn for a family visit to see my loved one during the Thai New Year (Songkran) celebrations. I had the opportunity to experience The Dawn's exceptional care and services firsthand. The team at The Dawn is incredibly professional and dedicated to providing the highest quality of care and safety for our loved ones during their recovery journey.

The tranquil setting of the property, comfortable rooms, and diverse food options all contribute to a welcoming and supportive environment for clients. It is evident that the staff at The Dawn pays attention to every detail, ensuring that clients feel cared for and valued, even during special events and seasons.

Overall, my experience at The Dawn was truly positive, and I have full confidence in recommending this facility to others seeking a reputable and compassionate rehabilitation center.

After settling into my cozy room, I had time to relax before meeting the rest of the team and my peers.

The team at The Dawn is incredible—professional, compassionate, and always there when you need them. The support staff were ready to listen and hold space for me, my therapist Albert was not only extremely knowledgeable but truly passionate, and the doctors and nurses were top-notch. Then, there’s the fantastic gym team, the skilled massage therapists, and the people working behind the scenes—cooking delicious meals, maintaining the beautiful grounds, and keeping the whole place running smoothly.

You’ll meet peers from all over the world who truly understand your struggles. The treatment blends Western and Eastern approaches, giving you a holistic path to healing. Each day is packed with group sessions (where you gain valuable insights from peers), individual counseling, educational sessions on psychology, fitness classes (like yoga, pilates, gym workouts, walks, aqua fitness, pickleball, zumba), meditation, sound bowl sessions, and evening time for journaling, exploring emotions, and practicing gratitude and CBT.

If you’re struggling, don’t hesitate to ask for help. It’s not easy to face your fears and deepest, darkest secrets, but the relief that comes with shedding that weight is worth it. Don’t expect to walk out fully “healed”—this is real work, and it requires vulnerability. But with the incredible team at The Dawn guiding you, you’ll be equipped with tools that, if you continue to use them, can set you on the path to your best self for the future.

Just remember: from dusk till dawn, take it one day at a time, one step at a time.

I attended this facility seeking urgent clinical support during a severe crisis which was later followed by a significant mental health diagnosis. Prior to arrival, I communicated that I was experiencing a high level of distress and instability.

Based on my personal experience, I did not feel adequately assessed, supported, or stabilised during my stay. Instead, I left feeling more distressed than when I arrived, and the experience had a significant emotional and financial impact on me.

One of my main concerns was the difference between my expectations and my experience. The facility advertises personalised, trauma-informed care, but I personally found much of the treatment to be relatively generic and not sufficiently tailored to my individual circumstances. More than two weeks into my stay, I still did not have a clear treatment plan, had not had a one to one with a lead clinical specialist, and had received less productive one-to-one therapeutic support than I had expected based on my discussions during the admissions process.
I was also concerned by what I experienced as limited on-site medical support at the campus where I stayed. During my time there, I was not aware of any on site doctors, and my understanding was that residents requiring a higher level of medical support would be transferred to a local hospital.

There were also several practical issues that added stress during my stay, including:
• Inconsistent access to food and amenities. Food was available on a different campus which was only accessible at certain times, and I recall experiencing power cuts and issues with running water.
• Transport charges that I do not recall being clearly explained beforehand.
• Concerns about room cleanliness.
• Restrictions on personal coping strategies that I did not understand and which were never explained.
• An inability to change therapists despite requesting this.
• I did not receive feedback regarding complaints I raised.
• I can’t recall the refund policy being explicitly discussed with me during the admissions process.

I was disappointed that some of the specialised trauma-focused therapies I had expected were not available within the timeframe originally discussed before admission. During my stay, extending my admission was discussed as a way of accessing additional treatment. Personally, I found this frustrating given the significant financial commitment already involved.

The aspect I found most difficult was the feeling that my increasing distress during the admission process and my stay was not recognised in the way I had hoped. Looking back, I do not feel that the environment was the right fit for the level of support I needed at that time.

I did, however, meet several compassionate and supportive staff members, including a coordinator who was particularly helpful, and many members of the local support team treated me with kindness throughout my stay.

While others may have a different experience, this was mine. In my case, I did not feel safe, sufficiently assessed, or provided with the level of personalised care I had expected based on the facility's descriptions of its services.
